manifest.changelog:
* Money safety: paid mint quotes that were paid but never issued are now recovered instead of being lost
* Mint recovery is gated per mint, and mints are probed for reachability before they are used
* API keys and top-up tokens are stored before they are paid for, so a failed payment no longer loses the token
* Default mint is now Minibits, with cubabitcoin kept as a trusted mint
* A token is no longer lost when a source mint rejects it as untrusted; the client fails over to another mint
* Top-up estimates now account for the full request shape (tools, Responses input, image detail)
* Bounded NWC requests, so `nwc status` can no longer hang forever
* Canonical model IDs are now used for cooldowns and failover, so aliases like `claude-opus-5-5` resolve to nodes that list only `claude-opus-5.5`
* Added Nostr-sourced model ID mapping snapshots (kind 38426)
* Routed requests now forward `x-routstr-model-path`, adding DeepSeek model-path routing
* Upstream error responses are passed through to the client instead of being flattened
* Accept Anthropic `x-api-key` credentials
* Updated bundled routstrd to 0.4.12 and routstr-sdk to 0.4.8

manifest.title: Routstrd Auth
manifest.author: Routstr <hello@routstr.io>
manifest.description: Auth proxy and daemon for the Routstr AI routing network
manifest.tagline: Self-hosted Routstr node with bearer-token auth
manifest.changelog:
* Cloudron backups now snapshot the real SQLite database (`/app/data/routstrd/routstr.db`) through the WAL-aware sqlite addon instead of a raw filesystem copy of `/app/data`, so a backup taken while the daemon is writing is consistent and restores are not corrupt
* First-admin bootstrap works on a fresh install: `routstrd npubs register` can now read the empty npub store, so registering the first admin no longer fails with an auth error before it can POST
* Documented the first-admin registration flow and its caveat: while the store is empty the first `POST /npubs` is unauthenticated and claims the admin slot, so anyone who can reach the endpoint can claim it -- restrict access until registration is complete
* Provider mint awareness: the daemon discovers and caches which mints each provider accepts, and the client refuses mints a provider rejects and fails over on a mint shortfall or a top-up the wallet cannot fund, instead of losing the request
* A provider pin forced by the caller is now preserved during failover, and provider pinning is strict
* The API key is kept when an upstream request errors, and API keys a provider proves empty are dropped from the wallet
* Failover now sends forwarded API paths with the `/v1` prefix, and per-node unknown-path 404s fail over instead of failing the request
* Provider base URLs are now versioned and Anthropic models are rooted correctly for the `pi` integration
* The CLI normalizes remote URLs, retries the other loopback family, and no longer replays writes after an ambiguous connection failure (avoiding duplicate operations)
* History now shows which entries are waiting or cancelled
* Updated bundled routstrd to 0.4.14 and routstr-sdk to 0.4.9

* Startup now fails closed if the onboarding daemon cannot be stopped, so supervisord can no longer start while a stale daemon still holds the wallet PID lock

manifest.title: Routstrd Auth
manifest.author: Routstr <hello@routstr.io>
manifest.description: Auth proxy and daemon for the Routstr AI routing network
manifest.tagline: Self-hosted Routstr node with bearer-token auth
manifest.changelog:
* Auto-refill now checks the NWC balance before creating an invoice, and a refill invoice that times out is waited on until it reaches a final state before paying again, so a slow Lightning payment can no longer be paid twice
* Refund tokens the mint reports already spent are dropped, so they no longer linger in storage and inflate the held balance
* Mint recovery probes now hold their deadline even when fetch ignores the abort signal, so a down mint can no longer hold the recovery gate open
* Model and upstream-path cooldowns are now exponential: a qualifying failure cools its own scope for 10s, doubling per consecutive failure up to 10 minutes. Streaks survive cooldown expiry and restarts, `routstrd cooldowns --reset` clears them, and the CLI reports expiries, path scope and failure streaks
* Model-path resolution is spelling-aware: node `alias_ids` are retained and paths are merged across every spelling of a model, so a node advertising only a variant spelling is no longer dropped from routing. Added PPQ, Venice and Wafer DeepSeek routes
* Auto-pin failover now degrades to ordinary provider routing instead of exhausting the request; per-model path lookups are fetched once per spelling and cached, and each node gets a 6s ranking budget so one slow node's oversized path payload can no longer make every request pay its timeout
* Provider enable/disable reports the policy that actually took effect, backed by a two-tier Nostr review-label policy (default-enabled labels vs explicit opt-in)
* Unreachable providers can no longer stall discovery: provider fetches get an independent deadline (~3s instead of up to ~136s), model-path lookups are bounded, the four relay filters refresh concurrently, and unchanged model shards are skipped during incremental discovery
* Usage windows are now timezone-correct (IANA zone with DST-aware calendar arithmetic) and aggregate in SQL, cutting 7d over a 20k-row database from ~570ms to ~120ms
* Added time-window filtering across the TUI, including a window-driven History tab with a dual-axis spend/token chart
* The CLI prompts to update routstrd on start and restart, backed by daemon-side update state shared by the CLI and TUI, and added a `rout` alias for the binary
* Startup no longer repeats discovery work, and onboarding waits for a non-empty model list and warns instead of aborting when an integration installer fails
* Updated bundled routstrd to 0.4.17 and routstr-sdk to 0.4.12

manifest.description: Auth proxy and daemon for the Routstr AI routing network
manifest.tagline: Self-hosted Routstr node with bearer-token auth
manifest.changelog:
* Security: the image now runs Bun 1.4.4, whose bundled CA roots no longer include the compromised "emSign ECC Root CA - G3" and "AAA Certificate Services" roots. The daemon used to complete TLS handshakes with certificates chaining to those roots; browsers blocked them, but the daemon does not check revocation, so outbound calls to a forged endpoint could be intercepted. Those chains now fail to verify
* The system CA bundle in the image was refreshed at the same time and no longer carries the compromised roots either, so anything else in the container that uses the OS trust store is covered too
* Updated bundled routstrd to 0.4.18 and routstr-sdk to 0.4.13
manifest.postInstallMessage:
Routstrd Auth is now installed.

The app exposes an OpenAI-compatible Routstr endpoint protected by bearer-token auth. Persistent wallet/config/database data is stored under Cloudron's app data directory and included in backups.

If you need admin-only client management endpoints, set `routstrd remote <url>` and `routstrd npubs register` to register the first admin npub.

manifest.title: Routstrd Auth
manifest.author: Routstr <hello@routstr.io>
manifest.description: Auth proxy and daemon for the Routstr AI routing network
manifest.tagline: Self-hosted Routstr node with bearer-token auth
manifest.changelog:
* Security: a client API key can no longer read or delete provider credentials. `GET /keys/api` returned every upstream provider key in plaintext, and `POST`/`DELETE /keys/api/delete` refunded and removed them; both now require an admin npub over NIP-98, like the wallet sends. Any client key issued before this release could do both
* Security: client API keys are now limited to the endpoints Routstr Core itself forwards -- the inference routes (`chat/completions`, `completions`, `responses`, `messages`, `messages/count_tokens`, `embeddings`, `systemone`, `decisions`) and the image routes. Everything else returns 403, notably `GET /balance`, `/keys/balance`, `/providers`, `/providers/reviews`, `/cooldowns`, `/status`, `/version`, `/settings/*`, `/wallet/*` and `/requests/*`. Inference and image calls are unchanged; use NIP-98 from a registered npub for the rest
* Security: state-changing and value-moving wallet routes now require an admin npub instead of any registered npub: `POST /wallet/send/cashu`, `/wallet/send/bolt11`, `/wallet/sweep-offline`, `/wallet/send/cashu/<id>/mark-spent`, `/wallet/recover`, `/wallet/recover/operations`, `/wallet/unlock`, `/wallet/cleanup` and `/wallet/check-proofs`, plus the mint setters `POST /wallet/mints` and `/wallet/mints/default`. Reads stay open to every registered npub, including `routstrd wallet mints list` and `/wallet/mints/info`. `check-proofs` is not a read despite the name: it marks mint-reported proofs spent, which reclaims balance and finalizes reserved sends
* Security: `GET /usagePi` is no longer reachable through the proxy and now answers 404. The daemon route returned every client's usage rows for a chosen second without the npub scoping `/usage` applies, so any registered npub could read other clients' ids and spend; the route is also removed from routstrd itself, so an image that still bundles an old daemon is covered either way
* Security: request paths starting with `//` are rejected with 400. Bun collapsed the doubled slash when forwarding, so `//keys/api` reached the route the path check had just refused
* Per-npub monthly spend limits: an admin can set, clear and inspect a calendar-month sats cap for any npub, and spend is aggregated across the API keys that npub owns. A capped npub's paid requests are refused with 402 and `X-Routstr-Quota-*` headers until the month resets; management routes keep working. Paid NIP-98 requests are refused with 403 for a capped npub until usage can be attributed to them
* Operate it from the CLI with `routstrd npubs add/update --limit-sats`, `--clear-limit`, and `routstrd npubs list`, which shows each npub's cap and current-month spend
* Registering an npub now requires a display name. `POST /npubs` rejects a missing, null or whitespace-only name with 400, and `PATCH /npubs` refuses to clear one, so an identity can no longer be created nameless by any client. This covers the unauthenticated first-admin bootstrap too; a rejected attempt does not consume the bootstrap slot. Entries bootstrapped from `ROUTSTRD_AUTH_ADMIN_*` or migrated from the legacy admin table may still be unnamed, and startup logs a warning listing them
* The image now runs `cloudron/base` 6.0.1 (Ubuntu 26.04) instead of 5.0.0, which drops the inherited CRITICAL vulnerabilities from 133 to 14 and the image size from 2.87 GB to 1.34 GB; the 14 that remain are all inherited from Cloudron's base and are recorded with statements and expiries in `.trivyignore.yaml`
* Every release image is now scanned by Trivy before it is pushed, and the push is gated on the result. A CRITICAL that is neither fixed nor accepted with an expiry blocks the release
* The app now requires Cloudron 10.1.1 or newer. The image moved from Ubuntu 24.04 to 26.04 in this release, which is the first time the platform underneath it has changed; Cloudron older than 10.1.1 has not been tested against it and is no longer offered this version. Boxes below the floor keep running their current version, and Cloudron reports the requirement when they try to update
* Updated bundled routstrd to 0.5.0 and routstr-sdk to 0.5.1
* routstrd 0.5.0 brings no-swap offline Cashu sends with manual settlement and a confirmed sweep for the ones that aged out, a periodic in-flight melt sweep with expired-quote rollback and rollback-aware melt history, recovery of paid NPC quotes and parked refund tokens, a cap on offline-send overpayment with an online fallback, and protection against a cancelled request starting wallet funding
* It also adds persistent per-request lifecycle logs -- `routstrd logs` now shows one line per request with retries and failovers, with `--verbose`, `--follow`, filters and lifecycle trace routes -- an `auto-model-path` toggle applied without a restart, a compact route-first view of automatic model-path candidates, provider lists that hide unreachable nodes unless `--all` is passed, and a repair step for stale macOS code signatures on the standalone binary
manifest.postInstallMessage:
Routstrd Auth is now installed.

The app exposes an OpenAI-compatible Routstr endpoint protected by bearer-token auth. Persistent wallet/config/database data is stored under Cloudron's app data directory and included in backups.

If you need admin-only client management endpoints, set `routstrd remote <url>` and run `routstrd npubs register --name "Your Name"` to register the first admin npub. A display name is required, and the CLI prompts for one if you leave the flag out.

manifest.title: Routstrd Auth
manifest.author: Routstr <hello@routstr.io>
manifest.description: Auth proxy and daemon for the Routstr AI routing network
manifest.tagline: Self-hosted Routstr node with bearer-token auth
manifest.changelog:
* The image no longer ships the inherited C/C++ build toolchain. `build-essential`, the `gcc`/`g++`/`cpp` compiler packages, `binutils`, `make`, `libc6-dev` and `linux-libc-dev` are purged after the dependencies are installed, which removes 17 of the 18 CRITICAL vulnerabilities the image used to carry. Nothing in the app compiles anything at runtime: Bun, the `routstrd` daemon and the auth proxy are all prebuilt. The one remaining CRITICAL is `gosu`'s Go standard library, inherited from the Cloudron base image and still recorded with a statement and expiry in `.trivyignore.yaml`. The image size is unchanged, because files removed from inherited layers still occupy those layers
* Release reports now show what is actually in the image. Accepted findings used to be filtered out of the Trivy report, so a release report looked identical to a clean image; the full report now retains them with the acceptance statement that covers each one, and the summary counts unaccepted, accepted, introduced and dependency findings separately. What blocks a release is unchanged
* The security gate now warns before an acceptance expires (30 and 7 days out, and once it has expired) and when an acceptance no longer matches anything the scans report, instead of that surfacing as a blocked release
* The gate fails closed. A scan that errors, a missing lockfile or an unusable report now stops the release with a distinct exit code rather than being read as a pass, and `.trivyignore.yaml` is validated before any scan starts
* Updated bundled routstrd to 0.5.0 and routstr-sdk to 0.5.1
